newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH-US ECK COMPLETES POWER DEAL WITH ABB.
newsitem.headline: CZECH-US ECK COMPLETES POWER DEAL WITH ABB.

text.p: ECK Generating sro, a Czech-U.S. joint venture, said on Friday it had completed a contract making Asea Brown Boveri's Czech unit the general contractor in building a new $400 million, 350 megawatt power plant in the Czech Republic.

"ECK Generating signed a contract today with the general contractor, ABB Energeticke Systemy s.r.o.," ECK said in a statement. "The value of investments on the basis of this project is 400 million dollars."

ECK Generating is partly owned by Independent Power CZ, a unit of California- based ACT Inc, with involvement also of NRG Energy, a subsidiary of U.S. power utility Northern States Power Co , and Nations' Energy Corp. a subsidiary of Tucson Electric Power Co. .

ECK said the project, near the city of Kladno northwest of Prague, would be financed by 15-year credits from the International Finance Corporation (IFC), Japan's Nissho Iwai Corporation, and Czech banks Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s. (CSOB) and Ceska Sporitelna a.s. .
It would also have equity financing in the form of a share capital increase of $100 million by the existing owners.
The IFC is granting $85 million in credits, Nissho Iwai $65 million, with CSOB and Sporitelna combining to provide $115 million in credit.
ABB also will provide a credit of $37.5 million, ECK said.
ECK has already signed a 20-year contract to supply power to the distribution company Stredoceska Energeticka a.s. from the plant, which is to be completed in 1999.
The ECK plant will also provide communal heating, from the combined coal/gas plant, to the city of Kladno.
